demoDress.name: Dress Journey — Camille
demoDress.description: Discover how Gally transforms the e-commerce search experience, following Camille, a customer looking for the perfect dress.

1.title: The arrival
1.bubble:
Camille searches for "tank dress" — a vague query. Autocomplete understands the intent and surfaces relevant results via vector search.
📊 Tracking: Gally logs a SEARCH event with the query, result count, and page. This surfaces popular searches, flags zero-result queries, and improves autocomplete.

2.title: The exploration
2.bubble:
Camille browses summer dresses. Facets — color swatches, price slider, search within options — help her find exactly what she wants, with no bounce.
📊 Tracking: Gally logs VIEW:category (category visit) and DISPLAY (products shown with their position). This measures category performance and each product's impression rate.

3.title: The doubt
3.bubble:
The merchant hesitates: how do you steer ranking without a developer? Gally's Explain Query reveals how each product is ranked — boosts, text fields, relevance score — all controllable with no code.
📊 Tracking: SEARCH, DISPLAY, and ADD_TO_CART data collected continuously let Gally compute a per-product popularity score, usable as a merchandising boost criterion.

4.title: The decision
4.bubble:
Camille adds a dress to her cart. Average-order-value levers kick in: −20% accessory pack, free-shipping threshold, frequently bought together.
📊 Tracking: Gally logs ADD_TO_CART for every product added — a strong conversion signal that boosts the product in results. VIEW:product and ADD_TO_CART combined feed the recommendations.

5.title: The recap
5.bubble:
What's the business impact? How much time and budget to get there? See the cost/time vs. market recap.
📊 Tracking: The ORDER event closes the full loop: products bought together feed the "Frequently bought together" recommendations, and revenue per query optimizes relevance.
